title: Your company brain will leak secrets: how we stopped it for big banks — Tanmai Gopal, PromptQL
talk_summary: Tanmai Gopal argues that a 'company brain' should be a single company-wide markdown wiki with per-page scopes, where agents suggest memory additions that a named human accepts or rejects, rather than agents auto-writing memory or people hand-maintaining shared skill repos. He extends this to multi-user shared agents by never storing credentials in the sandbox and instead injecting the acting user's credentials at the HTTP/SQL layer so the agent acts as that human.

takeaways.technique: Agent-suggested, human-accepted wiki writes with per-page scopes
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of letting agents auto-write memory or asking people to hand-edit shared skill repos, the agent proposes a short bullet list of facts plus scopes, and the human clicks accept; every entry is attributed to a named person.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to get the agent to suggest a change instead of doing the change
takeaways.numbers: ~5,000 interconnected wiki pages in their own company brain

takeaways.technique: Per-file scopes tied to the acting user's claims
takeaways.what_they_do: Each wiki page carries read/write scopes; when an agent reads context it does so using the requesting user's claims, so it only sees what that person could see.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent is always using the user's credential to read the right part of the wiki

takeaways.technique: No credentials in the sandbox; inject user credentials at HTTP/SQL layer
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than baking credentials into the agent sandbox, they proxy/virtualize data and tool access and inject the acting user's credentials at the HTTP or SQL layer, so the agent behaves as that human for that interaction.
takeaways.evidence_quote: never store credentials in the sandbox. Instead of that at the HTTP layer, at the SQL layer, inject the user's credentials

takeaways.technique: Multi-person threads as the highest-quality context source
takeaways.what_they_do: They observe that the best brain entries come from two people arguing through a problem until the real root cause and decision are documented, not from single-agent auto-summaries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: When two people talk to each other and solve a problem, it creates the highest quality context

takeaways.technique: Grow the brain incrementally per owner, don't big-bang build it
takeaways.what_they_do: They reject a top-down 'build the company brain' project and instead have each person who does a slice of work own and grow their slice, expecting daily update volume to rise as the system proves useful.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're going to grow a company brain. We're not going to build one
takeaways.numbers: daily updates trended gently upward over two months
